text:
Andrei Svechnikov had no goals in eight games, then scored three in two nights, including two in the 9-2 rout of Chicago. His second, with 12.5 seconds left, tied the franchise record for goals in a game since relocation, as Cory Lavalette of the North State Journal noted.

Across the season the picture is steady. He has 9 goals on 8.8 expected, 18 points in 19 games, and Carolina gets 62% of the expected goals at five on five with him on. That's honest scoring on a team that controls play.

Evolving-Hockey's read from last season is the interesting part: he drove play at the 94th percentile, but his results lagged his chances badly (1.5 expected wins, 0.4 actual), and opponents also got more with him on the ice than with most forwards. This season the finishing has caught up. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking has him as more of a setup man than his reputation suggests, at the 86th percentile for primary shot assists. Watch whether the goals keep matching the chances; for the first time in a while, they are.
headline: Svechnikov's quiet month ended loudly
